occurrence_evidence.claim: SASSA directed notified recipients to complete life certification within a stipulated period. Its 10 April statement warned that non-completion could lead to delayed or suspended payment.
Interagency interface glitches prevented some notified beneficiaries from completing online eLife certification and caused office queues and transport burdens.
SASSA announced on 10 April that access had been restored and encouraged beneficiaries with the means to use the online portal.
On 23 April, IOL reported persistent facial-scan, OTP and Home Affairs failures. SASSA cited 13,644 successful verifications among 15,499 users by 16 April while acknowledging intermittent downtime.
May reporting gave 67,868 quarterly suspensions across mixed non-compliance causes and 7,779 facial-system complaints. Failed facial checks could be redirected to office fingerprints.
A separate August account says Sonel’s existing Old-Age Grant was withheld without notice before her attempts to resolve the problem through biometric verification.
In that August account, two fingerprint-capture attempts failed. The second followed a seven-hour clinic wait.
Sonel reported referral to Home Affairs for HANIS verification and an earliest available appointment in September. She anticipated at least two months without grant income.
